literal: Even begging resembles indeed giving, towards those who do not know hiding even in a dream.
translation: Begging from those who do not know how to hide their wealth, even in their dreams, is as pleasant as giving itself.
modern: கனவிலும் பிறருக்குக் கொடுப்பதை மறைக்கத் தெரியாதவர்களிடம் சென்று இரப்பதும், பிறருக்குக் கொடுப்பதைப் போன்ற பெருமை உடையதே ஆகும்.
explanation: This couplet explains that begging is not always a degrading act; its nature depends entirely on whom one asks. When a person begs from generous souls who cannot even conceive of hiding their wealth or refusing a request, even in their dreams, that act of receiving becomes as beautiful and dignified as giving itself. The key word 'கரத்தல்' refers to the act of concealing one's resources to avoid giving, and 'தேற்றாதார்' describes those who are completely incapable of such deceit. Thus, asking from such noble givers brings no shame, only joy.
